newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crude business stilled, offers steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crude business stilled, offers steady.

text.p: Foreign crude business into the U.S. failed to elicit much activity Monday, as the status quo ruled the session keeping dealings subdued.
Wet trades were concentrated on a few North Sea cargoes trading hands, featuring a steady wet Brent at December paper minus 48 cents and a dated-related Brent transaction.

U.S. dealers could muster little to say about the trans-Atlantic trade. Arbitrage opportunities remained weak, hovering at 70-75 cents for January WTI/Brent and at a more profitable 90-95 cents for the corresponding February months.
Slim arb numbers have allowed U.S. domestic grades to retain strength, filling refiner needs for sweet barrels.
Traders said Nigerian Qua Iboe was offered into the U.S. Gulf Coast at January WTI plus $1.00 for 500,000 barrels.

On the paper trading front, only a few Brent spreads were done, the latest a December/January Brent at plus 21 cents. Earlier in the day, the same spread sold 4-10 cents firmer between plus 25-31 cents.
U.S. aftermarket dealings also saw partial Brent outright trades for January at $22.90, unchanged from the IPE settlement.
A couple of Dubai January/February paper spreads were also heard sold at plus 49 cents and plus 50 cents, traders said.
